costGuide.title: Land Rover 448DT Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 448DT typically takes 18-24 hours at £65/hr (independent) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes .
paragraphs: The primary cost driver for a 448DT engine replacement is the condition of the cooling and lubrication systems. Units with documented replacement of the valley oil cooler gaskets and upgraded aluminium coolant crossover pipes command a slight premium but carry significantly lower long-term risk. Because this is a complex twin-turbo V8, a full 448DT rebuild is more labour-intensive than inline alternatives, though its robust bottom-end design yields a high rebuild success rate. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for a detailed breakdown of what influences your final quote.

failures.title: Land Rover 448DT Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Oil Cooler Leaks (Valley of V8)
items.whatHappens: The oil cooler is situated in the valley of the V8. Over time, the seals and gaskets degrade due to constant heat cycling, allowing engine oil to leak into the valley. This can lead to severe oil loss, smoke from the engine bay, and in extreme cases, a fire risk if oil contacts hot exhaust components.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the oil cooler seals is a routine, labour-intensive but highly effective repair. If ignored and oil starvation occurs, catastrophic bearing failure can result, necessitating a full 448DT engine replacement.

items.title: Coolant Crossover Pipe Degradation
items.whatHappens: The plastic coolant crossover pipes running across the top of the engine become brittle with age and heat. They eventually crack, leading to rapid, often invisible coolant loss and severe engine overheating.
items.repairVsReplace: Upgrading to machined aluminium crossover pipes is a standard and highly recommended preventative repair. If overheating has occurred and caused cylinder head warping, a full unit replacement is required.

items.title: Alternator and Accessory Drive Failure
items.whatHappens: The high electrical load combined with the intense heat trapped in the V8 valley causes premature wear on the alternator and associated pulleys.
items.repairVsReplace: Alternator replacement is a straightforward and relatively inexpensive repair. It rarely requires engine replacement on its own, but a failing alternator can mask or exacerbate other electrical gremlins in the vehicle.

failures.goodYearsLine: Unlike its predecessor (the 3.6L 368DT), the 448DT has no catastrophic bottom-end design flaw. It is widely considered a durable, highly repairable engine when proactive cooling and oil system maintenance is performed .
failures.cta: Compare rebuilt 448DT prices with the failure already addressed

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 448DT
variants.intro: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically visible on the passenger side near the oil filter housing, or listed on the VIN plate under the bonnet. The 448DT is frequently confused with its predecessor, the Land Rover 368DT (a 3.6L V8 with a known catastrophic crankshaft fracture risk), or its petrol counterpart, the Land Rover 508PS (a 5.0L supercharged V8). Fitting a 368DT or 508PS into a 448DT vehicle requires different ECU mapping, turbo plumbing, and engine mounts, making exact code matching critical to avoid costly installation errors and repeat failures.

relatives.description: - the 3.6L TDV8 the 448DT replaced, which suffered from known timing chain tensioner and crankshaft fracture risks that the 4.4L architecture largely resolved.
- the 5.0L supercharged V8 that took over the flagship performance role in later models, marking the end of the V8 diesel line for Land Rover.
- the 3.0L TDV6/SDV6 that served as the more fuel-efficient alternative in the same chassis, though buyers should note it carries its own well-documented crankshaft bearing vulnerabilities.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 448DT - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 448DT is only advisable for lower-value hosts or project builds, and must come with verifiable proof that the oil cooler seals and coolant crossover pipes have been recently replaced. Without this documented history, the risk of inheriting a leaking or overheating engine is unacceptably high. Explore our vetted used 448DT engines

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned 448DT directly addresses the core weaknesses of this generation. It will include new oil cooler gaskets, upgraded aluminium coolant crossover pipes, and a thorough flush of the cooling system. This is the most sensible, cost-effective route for preserving a Discovery 4 or Range Rover without the unpredictability of a used unit. Compare reconditioned 448DT options

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified for high-mileage examples showing early signs of wear, or if the engine has already suffered overheating damage. A quality rebuild should include line-boring, new pistons and rings, and a complete overhaul of the valvetrain and turbochargers to exceed factory specifications. Discuss a custom 448DT rebuild

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network of vetted UK Land Rover specialists can supply the unit and handle the complex installation, backing the work with a nationwide warranty so you have a single point of contact for the entire job. View supply and fit options
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For typical host vehicles like the 2012-2020 Range Rover L405 or Range Rover Sport L494, current market values often sit between £18,000 and £55,000 . With reconditioned replacement costs starting around £6,000, the replacement is generally financially viable ( Safe). However, for late-model Discovery 4 L319 examples where values may dip closer to £10,000, if the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

items.question: What is the most common failure on the 448DT?
items.answer: The dominant failure patterns on the 448DT are oil cooler leaks in the valley of the V8 and coolant crossover pipe degradation. The oil cooler seals degrade due to constant heat cycling, leading to oil loss and potential fire risks if oil contacts hot exhaust components. Plastic coolant crossover pipes become brittle with age, causing rapid coolant loss and severe overheating. Unlike its predecessor, the 448DT has no catastrophic bottom-end design flaw, making it highly durable when these cooling issues are addressed.

items.question: Which Land Rover models use the 448DT engine?
items.answer: The 4.4L 448TD V8 diesel was fitted to the Land Rover Discovery 4 (L319), Range Rover (L405), and Range Rover Sport (L494) between 2010 and 2020. It served as the flagship diesel option, offering massive low-end torque and superior towing capacity compared to the V6 alternatives. It is mechanically distinct from the older 3.6L 368DT and the petrol 5.0L variants. Always verify your specific chassis code before ordering a replacement unit.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 448DT engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned 448DT is strongly recommended over a used unit to proactively address the known cooling system weaknesses. Used units carry a high risk of inheriting degraded oil cooler seals or brittle coolant crossover pipes. Proper reconditioning upgrades these specific weak points with new gaskets and machined aluminium crossover pipes. Reconditioned units come with a 12 to 24-month warranty, unlike the 3-6 months typical for used engines.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the 448DT and not the 368DT or 508PS?
items.answer: You can confirm your engine code by checking the VIN plate under the bonnet or the stamped code on the engine block near the oil filter housing. The 448DT is a 4.4L twin-turbo diesel, visually distinct from the older 3.6L TDV8 and the 5.0L supercharged petrol V8. Fitting the wrong revision will cause severe ECU mapping, turbo plumbing, and engine mount compatibility issues.
